source: Microsoft's documented eShop reference-application architecture (the .NET microservices reference): bounded contexts / services + shared building blocks + client apps + Aspire orchestration host.

source_artifacts.diagram: img/eshop_architecture.png — Microsoft's published 'eShop reference application' diagram (the authoritative primary source; embedded by README.md). Visually confirms the service decomposition and the OrderProcessor-in-Order-Service fold; does NOT itself draw the BuildingBlocks grouping (Event Bus is a standalone element, the other three infra libs are not depicted), which is why that cluster is the one judgment no syntactic signal recovers.
source_artifacts.readme: README.md — 'A reference .NET application implementing an e-commerce website using a services-based architecture using .NET Aspire.'
source_artifacts.learn_doc: https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/architecture/microservices — '.NET Microservices: Architecture for Containerized .NET Applications' (the broader reference guidance eShop is the canonical sample for).
source_artifacts.pinned_at: All in-repo artifacts cited at dotnet/eShop commit 9b4f943 (subject_version above).

construction.services: Each documented service maps to its project(s): Catalog=Catalog.API; Basket=Basket.API; Identity=Identity.API; Payment=PaymentProcessor; Webhooks=Webhooks.API+WebhookClient. Ordering is the documented DDD bounded context spanning Ordering.API + Ordering.Domain + Ordering.Infrastructure + the OrderProcessor background worker.
construction.webapps: WebApp + WebAppComponents (Blazor storefront) + ClientApp + HybridApp (.NET MAUI clients) -> WebApps.
construction.building_blocks: EventBus + EventBusRabbitMQ + IntegrationEventLogEF + eShop.ServiceDefaults -> BuildingBlocks (documented cross-cutting infrastructure).

format: RSF `contain <cluster> <csproj-id>` tuples; entity ids are the `csharp:csproj:<repo-rel-path>` ids the target-granularity graph export emits.
rater_agreement: Original transcription (2026-06): single transcriber from the public eShop architecture docs. The service->project mapping is near-mechanical (the repo's project names mirror the documented services); the only judgement calls are grouping the four building blocks together and folding OrderProcessor into the Ordering context (both documented). Independent re-derivation by two blind raters done 2026-07-21 (eval §5.3 / §10a W3a) — see `independent_raters` below.

independent_raters.protocol: eval §10a / docs/rq9-blind-curation-runbook.md §5 (the W3a revalidation): two raters re-derived this reference independently from the pinned checkout + the project's public docs, blind to reference.rsf, to each other, and to all tool output; the pre-consensus worksheets are frozen (κ + the RQ9 ceiling row come from those); reconciliation to a consensus happened afterwards.
independent_raters.artifacts: references/eshop/blind-curation/ — worksheet-R-C.csv + worksheet-R-D.csv (frozen), rater-R-C.rsf + rater-R-D.rsf, ceiling.json, worksheet-consensus.csv + consensus.rsf, attestation-*.md (name-redacted), worksheet-target.csv (the entity list the raters got).

agreement.note: κ is computed on normalized labels (pre-registered, eval §10a.6) and is 0.0 because the two raters shared no label string at all ('Basket' vs 'BasketService', 'View' vs 'WebApp', …) — the pre-registered κ<0.6 flag therefore fired for VOCABULARY, not structure. Partition agreement is what MoJoFM/a2a measure: R-D's 13-cluster partition is a strict refinement of R-C's 8-cluster one — zero cross-boundary conflicts; all disagreement is granularity, concentrated in the undocumented shared-infrastructure tier (EventBus, EventBusRabbitMQ, IntegrationEventLogEF, ServiceDefaults, AppHost) and the frontend split. Every documented service was grouped identically by both raters.

R-C.delta: identical up to merging Orchestration (AppHost) into the BuildingBlocks cluster; reuses the documented service names

R-D.delta: a strict refinement (WebApps → 3 clusters, BuildingBlocks → 3); every documented service intact

consensus.relation_to_committed: strict refinement of the committed 9-cluster reference (WebApps → WebApp / WebAppComponents / ClientApp / HybridApp; BuildingBlocks → EventBus / Logging / ServiceDefaults; Orchestration = AppHost); 0 cross-boundary conflicts; R-C's 'Data' label resolved to Webhooks.

scored_reference_decision.decision: The committed GT-doc reference (this directory's reference.rsf, 9 clusters) REMAINS the scored reference for RQ1/RQ2/RQ9 — per the pre-registered rule (companion plan §9 Q4 / runbook §8 Phase 2: it stays unless κ reveals REAL disagreement).
scored_reference_decision.rationale: The κ flag fired on label vocabulary alone (labels_shared=0) while partition agreement with the committed reference is high (R-C: MoJoFM 93.1, a2a 97.9) and the consensus is a strict refinement with zero boundary conflicts — granularity, not real disagreement. Switching to the finer consensus after the fact would move every eShop number for a reason the pre-registration does not recognise.
reporting: the consensus is reported as the W3a independent re-derivation result: it reproduces the committed reference up to refinement, 0 conflicts
RQ9 additionally reports the blind curator vs the consensus as a clearly-labelled SENSITIVITY row (projection=vs-consensus), never the headline
the κ=0.0 ceiling is reported as pre-registered, beside MoJoFM/a2a, with the vocabulary explanation

caveats: Small system (19 projects, 9 clusters): most services are a single project, so target-granularity clustering is partly trivial. The discriminating cases are the multi-project Ordering DDD context and whether dependency-only baselines keep the microservice boundaries (they tend not to, via the shared building blocks).

The curation overlay is FINER than this reference in places (separate Event Bus / Integration Event Log / Service Defaults containers vs. the documented BuildingBlocks group; OrderProcessor as its own container vs. folded into Ordering) — an honest granularity disagreement that lowers MoJoFM, not a tool error.
C# target granularity only (no per-document Roslyn references yet).
